courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course introduces students to the Workplace Hazardous Materials Management System (WHMIS), WorkSafeBC regulations, proper use of personal protection equipment, procedures for using fire extinguishers and the use of vehicle hoisting, and lifting equipment. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.
This course introduces you to the roles and responsibilities of employees, employers, and customers, as well as shop efficiency and management and creating written reports. Prerequisite(s): AUTO 1500
This course introduces you to various general hand and power tools, measuring instruments, threaded fasteners. Prerequisite(s): AUTO 1500

This course introduces students to the principles of electricity, electrical schematics, diagnostic tools andprocedures, power sources, and hybrid and electric vehicle safety. Prerequisite(s): AUTO 1500
This course introduces you to specialty tools and equipment, service and repair techniques, wear and failure diagnostic analysis, and maintenance procedures. Prerequisite(s): AUTO 1500
This course introduces you to safety, equipment shut down and storage, oxy-acetylene torches and metal inert gas, and heating, cutting, and welding. Prerequisite(s): AUTO 1500
This course introduces students to the principles of hydraulics and friction, service and repair techniques for brake components, and disc and drum brake systems. Prerequisite(s): AUTO 1500
This course introduces students to specialty tools and equipment, service and repair techniques for suspension systems. Prerequisite(s): AUTO 1500

This course introduces you to specialty tools and equipment, steering component overhaul, wheel alignment requirements, and service and repair techniques for steering systems. Prerequisite(s): AUTO 1500

This course introduces you to an overview of the internal combustion engine, engine management systems, and acquiring an understanding of vehicle emissions and their impact on the environment. Prerequisite(s): AUTO 1500

This course introduces you to the use of lubricants and fluids, procedures for measuring fluid levels and condition, replacing fluids and their maintenance requirements, identifying sources of leaks, replacing gaskets and seals, and servicing body components. Prerequisite(s): AUTO 1500

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This work practicum allows students the opportunity to gain practical experience at a sponsoring automotive repair facility. This real life, automotive-related work experience reinforces materials presented in the program and enhances skills and abilities through interaction with experienced tradespeople. This 2 week work practicum may not be consecutive weeks. The time frame of the work practicum will be determined by the instructor through consultation with industry partners. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

​This course introduces students to the use of lubricants and fluids, procedures for measuring fluid levels and condition, replacing fluids and their maintenance requirements, identifying sources of leaks, replacing gaskets and seals, and servicing body components. Prerequisite(s): AUTO 1500

admission.raw: Scheduled intakes September each year Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year. Entrance requirements This program has a two-step admission process. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. When available intakes are full, qualified applicants are wait-listed. Step 1: Pre-entry assessment Applicants must complete a pre-entry assessment form to have their experience and interest assessed by the program area. Submit your completed Pre-entry Assessment form [PDF] to auto-foundation@bcit.ca . Potential applicants will be contacted to attend an informational orientation with the program area. Once your pre-entry assessment form has been signed by the program area, you can upload it and submit your online application. Step 2: Meet the following entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements prior to applying to this program. If you are uncertain or don’t meet the requirements, we strongly recommend you complete any applicable Trades Entry Assessments before applying. English language proficiency: one of: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent or BCIT English Trades Entry Assessment Math: one of the following: Foundations of Math and Pre-Calculus 10 (50%) or Workplace Math 10 (50%) or Other acceptable BC and Yukon courses or BCIT Math Trades Entry Assessment Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Recommended for success Applicants are encouraged to register for an in-person program orientation at the Burnaby campus. Potential students with medical or physical disabilities should contact Accessibility Services to arrange an interview with the institute's rehabilitation specialist at 604-451-6963 (telephone interview is acceptable for out-of-town applicants). A valid driver’s license or a minimum “N” designation is needed for practicum completion. International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks.
